item.title: [8] Universal electrical resistivity in iron-based high-temperature superconductors
item.description:
Last authors: E. F. Talantsev

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant to unconventional superconductivity (Fe-based, cuprates, nickelates) and nematic order, experimental observable.

Tags: #superconductivity #nematicity #transport #cuprates #iron-based

Abstract: Temperature-dependent electrical resistivity $\rho(T)$ in cuprate, iron-based, and nickelate superconductors represents one of unresolved problems in modern solid-state physics, because of the high absolute value of $\rho(T)$, which, in many cases, exceeds the Ioffe-Rigel criterion, and a large difference in the $\rho(T)$ shape for samples with different doping. Here I show that the nearest neighbors parallel resistivity model (arXiv: 2607.23484) can well describe the in-plane resistivity $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in iron-based superconductors (IBS) of type 11, 111, 122, 1111, 1144 and 42214 in which the spin density wave phase or nematic order is suppressed by doping. The model is based on the postulate that $\rho_{ab}(T)$ is a sum of two parallel conduction channels, where one channel is described by the Bloch-Gr\"uneisen equation and the other by the Arrhenius hopping equation. Consequently, the variety of $\rho_{ab}(T)$ in the IBS is explained as a variation of the Debye temperature $\Theta_D$ and the hopping activation energy $E_a$. The derived Debye temperatures were used to estimate the electron-phonon coupling constant $\lambda_{e-ph}$in the studied IBS.

item.title: [9] Two quantum spin liquid states coexisting in the kagome antiferromagnet herbertsmithite
item.description:
Last authors: Hong-Chen Jiang, Young S. Lee

Authors: Arthur C. Campello, Shengtao Jiang, Wei He, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct interest: kagome antiferromagnet, quantum spin liquid, inelastic neutron scattering experiment.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #kagome #quantumspinliquid #neutronscattering #antiferromagnet

Abstract: Herbertsmithite (ZnCu$_3$(OH)$_6$Cl$_2$) is one of the most extensively studied quantum spin liquid (QSL) candidates, yet the precise nature of its ground state remains unresolved. Here, we compare the results of high-resolution inelastic neutron scattering on single crystals of herbertsmithite (Zn$_\mathrm{x}$Cu$_\mathrm{4-x}$(OD)$_6$Cl$_2$, $x\simeq 0.85$) with large-scale density-matrix renormalization group (DMRG) and dynamical DMRG simulations to benchmark the spin Hamiltonian and uncover fundamental properties of the ground state. The measured spin correlations determine an energy density for the Heisenberg model that closely matches simulations, an essential verification of the Hamiltonian. In parallel, DMRG simulations reveal two nearly degenerate QSL states. Both preserve translational symmetry, but one retains the lattice point-group symmetries whereas the other develops anisotropic spin correlations that break point-group symmetry. These two QSLs have distinct spin structure factors, and, remarkably, close agreement with the neutron spectra is achieved with an admixture of the two states. Our results establish a quantitative correspondence between neutron scattering and simulations, and suggest that herbertsmithite realizes a regime in which two proximate gapped QSL states coexist.

item.title: [10] Monolayer van der Waals kagome lattice for high-temperature flat-band physics (Nat. Phys.)
item.description:
Last authors: Kyle M. Shen, Mingu Kang

Authors: Hyungkun Bong, Choongjae Won, Seongyong Lee, et al.

Published as: Nat. Phys. DOI

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Chris Jozwiak

Tags: #ARPES #angle-resolvedphotoemission #photoemission #kagome #anomalousHall #moire #vanderWaals #monolayer

Abstract: Kagome lattice materials host a remarkably rich landscape of novel quantum phenomena, all arising from the intrinsic interplay of topology, correlation, and frustration. While previous studies have been mostly limited to bulk three-dimensional (3D) kagome crystals, the realization of a true two-dimensional (2D) kagome system has remained a long-standing goal, to unlock fundamentally new physics and engineering pathways inaccessible in 3D systems. In this work, we establish the first ideal 2D monolayer kagome lattices by leveraging a novel and versatile van der Waals (vdW) kagome family, A2T3X4 (A = K, Rb, Cs; T = Ni, Pd, Pt; X = S, Se). Our nano-focused angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (nano-ARPES) directly characterizes the electronic structure of A2T3X4 down to the monolayer limit, notably revealing an isolated kagome-derived flat band just below the Fermi level. Via gate-engineering of 2D A2T3X4, the kagome flat band can be further tuned to the Fermi level, allowing direct access to the partially filled flat band physics and establishing a qualitatively new 2D flat band platform. Compared to existing moire-based artificial flat band systems, this vdW kagome-based intrinsic flat band system realizes more than 220 times higher flat band electron density, opening an entirely new density and energy regime for exploring 2D flat band physics. Harnessing this high-electron-density flat band in 2D vdW kagome system provides a clear pathway to scale emergent flat band phenomena - such as fractional quantum anomalous Hall states - to far higher temperatures than currently achievable, as long-envisioned in theory and further supported by our many-body calculations.

item.title: [9] A Chiral Superlattice Route to Spin-Split Topological Antiferromagnetism (Nature)
item.description:
Last authors: Philip Kim, Su-Yang Xu

Authors: Thao Dinh, Mengke Liu, Jian-Xiang Qiu, et al.

Published as: Nature DOI

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct interest: topological antiferromagnetism, chiral superlattice, giant anomalous Hall, Berry curvature.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #topologicalmaterials #antiferromagnet #anomalousHalleffect #Berrycurvature #spintronics

Abstract: The interplay between chirality and magnetism is a profound topic, spanning particle physics, condensed matter, chemistry and origin of life. In this paper, we study this interplay in the new antiferromagnet (AFM) UOTe, and we report a chiral superlattice route to spin-split topological phenomena from collinear antiferromagnetism. Pristine UOTe is a collinear AFM without Berry curvature or spin-split bands. However, we identify the spontaneous formation of a chiral superlattice in UOTe, which can be viewed as frozen chiral phonons at finite wave vector. When electrons move through the chiral superlattice, their orbital Bloch wavefunction and quantum geometry are modulated by the strong chiral superlattice potential, generating large Berry curvature in the chiral superlattice, which we detect by the nonlinear Hall effect. At 150 K, the chiral superlattice induced Berry curvature couples to the collinear AFM order, generating a giant anomalous Hall angle ~0.14 abruptly near $T_N$ that is among the largest in bulk magnets. Moreover, our spin Hanle precession measurement shows that the chiral superlattice also generates spin-polarized current from the collinear AFM, a long-standing goal in spintronics. We shed light on the supermodulation formation mechanism based on chemical ion size and physical interlayer-intralayer energy competitions, using which we propose a design principle to discover similar bond-mismatch superlattices, providing a chiral superlattice pathway through real space engineering of quantum geometry.

item.title: [7] Charge disproportionation and spin ordering in LiV2O5 and NaV2O5: a distributed moment point of view
item.description:
Last authors: Mark van Schilfgaarde, Walter R. L. Lambrecht

Authors: Claudio Garcia, Ilteris K. Turan, Jerome Jackson, Swagata Acharya, Mark van Schilfgaarde, Walter R. L. Lambrecht

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Electronic structure and spin ordering calculations (QSGW) for real correlated materials.

Tags: #electronicstructure #bandstructure #magnetism #DFT #stronglycorrelated

Abstract: The effects of charge disproportionation between V$^{4+}$ and V$^{5+}$ on the exchange interactions and related magnetic, electronic and optical properties are studied in LiV$_2$O$_5$ and NaV$_2$O$_5$. The magnetic exchange interactions between local moments on atomic sites are calculated using a linear response approach based on the QS$GW$ band structure. While the induced magnetic moments are small on the vanadyl O$_v$ and bridge O$_b$, their exchange interactions with the V are found to be larger than between V atoms. The N\'eel temperature $T_N$ are calculated within the mean-field (MFA) and random phase (RPA) approximations for two different crystal structures with $P2_1mn$ and $Pmmn$ spacegroups. The critical temperatures are are corrected by a quantum statistical factor of (S+1)/S to obtain reasonable agreement with experiment. Band structures, optical dielectric functions calculated using the Bethe Salpeter Equation method and spin waves are also calculated and presented for both crystal structures and both compounds. The spin wave dispersions are calculated from the classical Heisenberg Hamiltonian including magnetic moments on both V and O atoms. Besides the lowest energy weakly interacting spin waves of the two chains of spins in the unit cell, the model predicts additional high energy optical spin waves, which correspond to more complex spin excitations in which the spins on the two V across a bridge, vanadyl O and bridge O precess independently from each other instead of staying locked together according to their collinear alignment in the ground state. These show only weak dispersion and extend up to about 1 eV but we argue that these are an artefact of using the Heisenberg model beyond its validity range and would be suppressed in a more complete theory that allows for coupling of the transverse spin with longitudinal spin and charge excitations.

item.title: [8] Second Chern Number Protected Gapless Vortex Modes in Superconducting Weyl Semimetals
item.description:
Last authors: Zhicheng Zhang, Jiangping Hu

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical study of gapless vortex modes in superconducting Weyl semimetals; high relevance to topological/superconductivity.

Tags: #Weylsemimetal #superconductivity #topological #theory #vortex

Abstract: We have studied the vortex bound states of superconducting linear and quadratic Weyl semimetals with time reversal symmetry. For vortex with vorticity $n$ (vortex line along $z$ direction) and Weyl semimetals with Weyl point chirality $\chi$, there are $\vert n\chi \vert$ gapless vortex modes around the location of each Weyl point in superconducting Weyl semimetals. We show that the appearance of $\vert n\chi \vert$ gapless vortex modes originates from the imbalanced pumping of flux bound states between Chern insulators obtained at $k_{z}$ and $-k_{z}$ in Weyl semimetals. Such a physical picture is verified by numerical calculations on lattice models. Moreover, the gapless modes around each Weyl point can be characterized by the second Chern number defined in a synthetic four-dimensional space based on the effective BdG Hamiltonian. Finally, these gapless vortex modes are found to be robust against rotational symmetry-breaking terms.

item.title: [9] Theory of High-Temperature Fractional Chern Phases in Monolayer van der Waals Kagome Materials A2T3X4
item.description:
Last authors: Mingu Kang, Gil Young Cho

Authors: Soomin Oh, Jiyong Han, Jinhyeok Choi, Donghae Seo, Mingu Kang, Gil Young Cho

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Directly identifies intrinsic topological flat bands in a new van der Waals kagome material family.

Tags: #material #kagome #topological #van-der-waals

Abstract: Fractional Chern insulators bring the fractional quantum Hall effect, with its anyonic excitations, to zero magnetic field. So far they have been realized in moir\'e materials, where the long superlattice period weakens electronic interactions and confines these phases to cryogenic temperatures. Early proposals instead envisioned topological flat bands on atomic-scale lattices, where fractionalization could persist to far higher temperatures, but a suitable material has been lacking. Here we theoretically identify monolayers of the recently synthesized van der Waals kagome family $\mathrm{A}_2\mathrm{T}_3\mathrm{X}_4$ as such a platform, combining intrinsic topological flat bands and strong Coulomb interactions with gate-tunable carrier density and layer assembly. Exact diagonalization of models derived from density functional theory reveals ferromagnetism over broad filling ranges, supporting diverse fractional Chern insulators, anomalous composite Fermi liquids, and charge-ordered phases. In particular, in $\mathrm{Cs}_2\mathrm{Pd}_3\mathrm{S}_4$, the fractional Chern insulator exhibits a many-body gap of approximately 26 meV in the largest system accessible with band mixing allowing at most one interband electron-hole excitation. Layer assembly further provides a natural route to fractional quantum spin Hall insulators: bilayers with antiparallel magnetizations support this phase at realistic separations. These results identify an experimentally accessible material family in which chemical composition, carrier density, and stacking offer complementary routes to fractionalization at enhanced energy scales and control over topological order.

item.title: [7] Vortexable Chern Bands Sit Exactly on the Topological Floor of Flat-Band Superfluid Stiffness
item.description:
Last authors: Zhi-Wei Wang, Samuel L. Braunstein

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theoretical treatment of flat-band superconductivity in Chern bands, relevant to moire and topological systems.

Tags: #theory #topology #superconductivity #moire

Abstract: Vortexable Chern bands host ideal fractional Chern insulators. Paired with time-reversed partners by orbital-diagonal on-site attraction, they are the least stiff flat-band superconductors at fixed Chern number $C$, filling, and pairing amplitude. For uniform pairing and a nondegenerate paired state, the exact $T=0$ stiffness determinant is the topological floor times $1+(\Torb/2\pi|C|)^2\le1+(\TLVP/2\pi|C|)^2$, where $\Torb$ and $\TLVP$ measure departures from vortexability. Enhancement costs vortexability, and the inequality is strict only if internal components share a site, as in heterostrained bilayers.

item.title: [8] Topological Splitting of Sondheimer Oscillations in Thin-Film Weyl Semimetals
item.description:
Last authors: Toshihito Osada

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Relevant topological transport theory for Weyl semimetals involving Berry curvature and Fermi surface effects.

Tags: #theory #topological-semimetal #transport #Berry-curvature

Abstract: We discuss topological effects on Sondheimer oscillations in the magnetoresistance of thin-film Weyl semimetals. The Sondheimer oscillations are periodic in magnetic field and originate from the commensurability between the film thickness and the cyclotron-orbit pitch. Using Boltzmann transport theory, we investigate the effects of Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment on the oscillations. We find that the Sondheimer oscillations split into two branches with different frequencies and that each branch becomes chirped because its frequency depends on magnetic field. These features originate from the orbital-Zeeman-induced deformation of the Fermi surface. The same mechanism also applies to Dirac semimetals.

item.title: [7] Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions and deconfined criticality in SrCu2(BO3)2
item.description:
Last authors: Yasir Iqbal

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$ linked to kagome Dirac spin liquids and experimental NMR signatures.

Tags: #theory #SrCu2(BO3)2 #spin-liquid

Abstract: SrCu$_2$(BO$_3$)$_2$ is the leading candidate for deconfined criticality, yet theories of its critical regime omit the Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya (DM) interactions, which gap the kagome Dirac spin liquid. Adding them to the SU(2) gauge theory, we show that time reversal and a spin-orbit-locked glide forbid any gauge-singlet spinon mass to all orders. In-plane DM only twists the spinons, reconstructing the nodes below $0.03$-$0.17$ K, while out-of-plane DM is irrelevant and SO(5) anisotropy arises only at second order. The material thus remains a platform for deconfined criticality, which NMR can test, since a $[100]$ field induces a N\'eel moment and a $[001]$ field does not.

item.description:
Last authors: Muntaser Naamneh (Department of Physics, Eran Maniv (Department of Physics

Authors: Matan Sterenberg (Department of Physics, Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Beer-Sheva 84105, et al.

Why: Experimental study of electrical switching in a van der Waals antiferromagnet Co$_x$TaS$_2$.

Abstract: Electrical switching in antiferromagnets is commonly described as the action of current-induced torques on a rigid order parameter. item.title: [9] Electric Hidden Unconventional Collinear Magnetism in 2D \(PT\)-Symmetric Antiferromagnets
item.description:

Abstract: Electric hidden unconventional collinear magnetism, in which a perpendicular electric field (\(\mathcal{E}_z\)) lifts the \(\mathcal{PT}\)-enforced degeneracy and selectively releases the hidden crystallographic constraints in conventional 2D antiferromagnets to drive emergent magnetic phases, has remained largely unexplored. item.description:
Last authors: Thomas Naimer, Jaroslav Fabian

Abstract: The three-dimensional topological insulator Bi$_2$Te$_3$ hosts topological Dirac states on its two-dimensional surfaces. Abstract: Recently, $\text{EuCd}_2\text{P}_2$ has attracted increased attention for its colossal magnetoresistive (CMR) property, the mechanism of which seems to deviate from that of known canonical CMR compounds such as manganites. Many studies underscore the role of low density of hole carriers caused by Eu vacancies, particularly in stabilizing ferromagnetic (FM) order and modifying electrical transport and magnetoresistive responses in this compound. Our Density Functional Theory (DFT) and Monte Carlo-based calculations reveal an oscillating ground state magnetic order as a function of electron carrier density. The ground state is found to be A-AFM metal for x=0.056, 0.125 and 0.5 while it becomes ferromagnetic metal at x= 0.33, 0.67 and 1. Most importantly, we predict colossal anisotropic magnetoresistance in this compound for x=0.125 and 0.5. Authors: Meysam Bagheri Tagani, Carmine Autieri, Sahar Izadi Vishkayi

Abstract: A weak or vanishing circular optical signal need not imply weak helicity-sensitive transitions: it can be the residual of much larger opposing microscopic contributions. We resolve the finite-frequency interband Kubo response before summing over transitions and momentum, separating cancellation among transitions at fixed momentum from cancellation across the Brillouin zone. An exactly compensated $d$-wave model establishes the symmetry benchmark. In MnTe, first-principles Wannier calculations reveal a symmetry-dark N\'eel orientation with an extended sign-changing circular kernel whose bulk integral vanishes. Reorienting the N\'eel vector removes this extinction, yet the allowed response remains a small imbalance between large positive- and negative-momentum sectors; the imbalance reverses with photon energy and flips the macroscopic sign. Thus magnetic symmetry decides whether circular response is allowed, whereas microscopic compensation determines how much survives and with what sign. This distinction provides a general framework for interpreting weak, vanishing, and sign-changing magneto-optical signals in compensated magnets.

item.title: [9] Magnetoelectric Bulk Photovoltaic Effect in Centrosymmetric Solids
item.description:
Last authors: Lei Zhang, Jian Wang

Authors: Longjun Xiang, Fuming Xu, Lei Zhang, Jian Wang

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Connects altermagnetism (RuF4) and Zeeman Berry curvature to experimental photovoltaic signatures.

Tags: #altermagnet #Berry-curvature #photovoltaic

Abstract: It is commonly believed that a bulk photovoltaic current requires broken spatial inversion symmetry. However, in this work, we demonstrate that dc photocurrents can arise in centrosymmetric solids from the bilinear coupling between the electric and magnetic components of light. This magnetoelectric bulk photovoltaic effect (MBPE) has a quantum-geometric origin in the dipole moments of the Zeeman quantum metric and Zeeman Berry curvature. We identify four distinct MBPE mechanisms, including time-reversal-even and time-reversal-odd injection-like and shift-like photocurrents driven by linearly or circularly polarized light. Our symmetry analysis shows that the MBPE is allowed in broad classes of two-dimensional centrosymmetric nonmagnetic and magnetic materials under normally incident light. As representative examples, we predict sizable MBPEs in centrosymmetric monolayer Pt$_2$HgSe$_3$ and altermagnetic RuF$_4$, with current densities on the order of $1~\mathrm{mA/m}$. Notably, the injection-like photocurrent in RuF$_4$ reverses sign upon switching either the light helicity or the N\'eel vector. Our results extend the bulk photovoltaic effect to centrosymmetric solids and open new opportunities for electrical readout of altermagnetic order.

Abstract: Altermagnets are an emerging class of magnetic materials that exhibit characteristic features of both ferromagnets and antiferromagnets. item.description:
Last authors: Sudeep Kumar Ghosh, Yogesh Singh

Why: muSR evidence of TRSB in a topological superconductor; very direct relevance to user interests.

Abstract: Centrosymmetric nonsymmorphic AB2 (A = Ru, Os) borides exhibit anomalous superconducting properties, but the microscopic nature of their superconducting ground state remains unresolved. Here, we investigate RuB2 using zero- and transverse-field muon spin relaxation (muSR), first-principles electronic-structure calculations, and Ginzburg-Landau symmetry analysis. Zero-field muSR reveals spontaneous internal magnetic fields below Tc = 1.6 K, providing direct evidence for time-reversal symmetry breaking (TRSB). Transverse-field measurements establish a fully gapped superconducting state, with a gap magnitude close to the BCS weak-coupling limit. Density-functional calculations show that RuB2 is a multiband Z2 topological metal with appreciable spin-orbit coupling. Guided by the experimental observations and the symmetry of the orthorhombic crystal structure, our Ginzburg-Landau analysis suggests that an internally antisymmetric, nonunitary spin-triplet state is a promising candidate for the superconducting order parameter. This candidate is consistent with both the observed TRSB and the fully gapped superconducting state. These results establish RuB2 as a promising platform for investigating unconventional superconductivity arising from the interplay of crystal symmetry, multiband electronic structure, and spin-orbit coupling, and motivate further studies of related nonsymmorphic borides. The two muSR measurements provide complementary constraints: zero-field data probe spontaneous magnetism associated with TRSB, while transverse-field data characterize superconducting field distribution and support a full gap. The topological electronic structure and spin-orbit coupling provide context for unconventional pairing. Although these results do not uniquely determine the order parameter, they narrow candidates and highlight that nonsymmorphic symmetry may shape superconductivity in RuB2.

Abstract: Extensive studies of hidden spin polarization have established a broad class of hidden phenomena in quantum materials. item.description:
Last authors: Giovanni Mattei, James K. Utterback

Authors: Ilaria Delbono, Raouf Amara, Matias Feldman, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Real-space imaging of phase boundary dynamics in a classic correlated electron system (VO2).

Tags: #experiment #VO2 #metal-insulator-transition

Abstract: Achieving a detailed picture of the nature and dynamics of phase boundaries remains a major challenge, particularly solid-solid transitions central to phase-change materials. Here, we use stroboscopic optical scattering microscopy and finite-element simulations to study the nonlinear thermally driven motion of the mesoscale insulator-metal phase boundary in VO2 thin films. We visualize the lateral spatiotemporal evolution of a diffraction-limited photoinduced metallic phase domain, resolving its outward propagation, contraction, and ultimate disappearance. The phase boundary dynamics are governed by heat flow, which can be controlled by excitation fluence, film thickness, and substrate thermal conductivity. Parameter-free agreement between the data and nonlinear thermal transport simulations identify the phase boundary transport as locally diffusive under this regime. We quantify how the latent heat acts as a thermal inertia, suppressing transport and prolonging the phase coexistence. Paradoxically, despite being driven by the underlying thermal gradient locally described by Fourier's law, the mesoscale phase front propagates faster than expected from thermal diffusion. This phenomenon arises from the distinction between temperature-field evolution and phase-boundary isotherm motion. These results establish a link between heat dissipation and mesoscale phase-front motion, providing a framework for controlling phase-transition kinetics relevant to photonics applications of VO2. We anticipate that this approach generalizes to a broad class of first- and second-order transitions.

Why: Experimental ultrafast spectroscopy on van der Waals heterostructures relevant to electronic dynamics.

Abstract: Transient absorption spectroscopy is a widely used technique for investigating ultrafast electronic dynamics, where transient optical signals are generally interpreted as arising from excitations within the material hosting the probed optical transition. A distinct form of transient absorption spectroscopy, termed proximity transient absorption (PTA), is demonstrated, in which the probed optical transition and the monitored photoexcited carriers reside in different materials. Using graphene/hBN/WS$_2$ heterostructures, photoexcited carriers in graphene induce a strong transient optical response at the excitonic resonance of a WS$_2$ monolayer through Coulomb screening, even when the two layers remain electronically isolated by an atomically thin hBN spacer. The resulting signal follows the carrier dynamics of graphene rather than those of WS$_2$, demonstrating that the WS$_2$ exciton acts as an optical transducer of electronic processes in a neighboring material. The signal decreases systematically with increasing hBN thickness, confirming its proximity origin while remaining substantial for separations approaching 2 nm. PTA provides a noncontact approach for optically modulating one material using photoexcited carriers in another and enables probing of carrier dynamics in materials that are otherwise difficult to investigate directly. More broadly, PTA establishes a new modality of ultrafast spectroscopy and reveals that transient optical signals in van der Waals heterostructures can originate from excitations residing in spatially separated layers.

Last authors: Indra Gankhuyag, Piers Coleman

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory of a specific heavy-fermion superconductor with parity transitions relevant to user interests.

Tags: #theory #heavyfermion #superconductivity #topological

Abstract: Spin triplet superconductors are of interest because of their topological properties, and their robustness to high magnetic fields. CeRh$_2$As$_2$ is a unique heavy fermion superconductor with both even-parity and candidate odd-parity superconducting phases with a special feature enabling a field induced phase transition between the two. The field induced transition which switches the parity of the Cooper pairs is enabled by a staggered antisymmetric spin orbit coupling (ASOC) interaction. However, the heavy fermion origins of the superconductivity in CeRh$_2$As$_2$ and the origin of the antisymmetric spin-orbit coupling are currently unexplored. Here, we develop a Kondo lattice model for CeRh$_2$As$_2$ and demonstrate how local hybridization between Cerium $d$- and $f$-orbitals, driven by the locally broken inversion symmetry, at the Cerium sites generates the ASOC. The resulting Kondo lattice model leads to nearly degenerate even and odd parity superconducting states that display a field induced parity transition between an even-parity state and an odd-parity pseudospin triplet state. We discuss the wider implications of our results extended to other heavy fermion systems like CeSiI.

item.title: [7] Quantum-interference correction to conductivity in disordered electronic bands with non-uniform quantum geometry
item.description:
Last authors: Asimpunya Mitra, Yong Baek Kim

Authors: Yip Chun Wong, Asimpunya Mitra, Yong Baek Kim

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Theory connecting quantum geometry and weak localization in graphene systems.

Tags: #theory #graphene #quantumgeometry #transport

Abstract: Weak localization in two-dimensional disordered electron systems originates from constructive interference between time-reversed scattering paths, giving rise to a logarithmically divergent quantum-interference correction to the dc conductivity. This behavior is generally suppressed when time-reversal symmetry (TRS) is broken. In this study, using a band-projected framework motivated by spin- and valley-polarized rhombohedral $N$-layer graphene (RNG), we show that nonuniform quantum geometry can qualitatively modify quantum-interference corrections to dc transport. In particular, continuously tuning the quantum geometry can change the sign of the conductivity correction, corresponding to a crossover between localization and antilocalization tendencies. Remarkably, at special values of the parameter controlling the quantum geometry, weak-localization (WL) or weak-antilocalization (WAL) can re-emerge despite broken microscopic TRS. At these special points, the orbital structure of the Bloch states gives rise to an emergent antiunitary symmetry that protects a gapless Cooperon mode and restores the logarithmically divergent quantum-interference correction characteristic of WL or WAL. Our results establish nonuniform quantum geometry as a mechanism for controlling quantum interference and electron localization in multiorbital electronic systems.

item.title: [9] CME-SpectrumBench: Can LLMs Analyze Condensed Matter Spectral Data?
item.description:
Last authors: Ion Stoica, Zhi-Xun Shen

Authors: Jin Gene Wong, Anjney Midha, Joseph Mathew Tennyson, Wei-Lin Chiang, Ion Stoica, Zhi-Xun Shen

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: Zhi-Xun Shen

Tags: #authorWhitelist

Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) are presently well assessed by expert-level mathematics and physics benchmarks which focus on theoretical, symbolic reasoning. However, we lack experimental benchmarks that evaluate data analysis in frontier research problems, a capability that future domain-specific foundation models must have. To this end, we present CME-SpectrumBench, an expert-designed benchmark consisting of 190 questions that measures how reliably frontier LLMs analyze research-level spectral scientific data in condensed matter experiments (CME). Using simulated CME spectral data, we prompt models to identify structures from 2D intensity arrays in the face of noise and limited instrumental resolution, a test of dense context reasoning. Models are scored by how accurately their numerical answers approach the ground truth. Under direct query, scores generally pale in comparison to handwritten code due to clear failure modes: models can find simple features but struggle to trace patterns or compute derived quantities, and performance typically degrades with increased data resolution and noise/convolution levels. LLM performance becomes comparable to handwritten code by allowing tool use (access to a Python interpreter) with/without ReAct prompting, in effect mapping questions onto agentic code generation problems. Our findings show that frontier models can serve as research assistants by interfacing with data through code, but still face difficulties processing information directly from large datasets - a key barrier future foundation models must overcome. The code and data are publicly available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/jingene/CMESpectrumBench.

item.title: [9] Certifying Nonlocal Spin Quantum Entanglement from Local Tunneling Spectra
item.description:
Last authors: Md. Shafayat Hossain, M. Zahid Hasan

Authors: Payman Kazemikhah, Ruolun Zhang, Xiangyu Luo, et al.

Score 9/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: author whitelist: M. Zahid Hasan

Tags: #authorWhitelist

Abstract: Quantum entanglement is intrinsically nonlocal, whereas tunneling spectroscopy measures one site at a time. We show that this apparent mismatch can be overcome: local tunneling spectra can certify spin entanglement without coherent control or absolute intensity calibration. An exact spin sum rule turns the high-bias conductance into an internal normalization, allowing the inelastic spin-flip weight to place a lower bound on the local quantum Fisher information. Total-spin conservation then fixes the otherwise inaccessible intersite fluctuation, converting two local spectra into a bound on a collective entanglement witness. We incorporate coupling to the substrate through a spectroscopic bound on spin leakage, while a hierarchy of thresholds distinguishes entanglement between the spins from entanglement with their environment. Including instrumental broadening and noise, the resulting certificate holds at a stated confidence level. These results establish a route for extracting nonlocal quantum information from equilibrium local spectroscopy.

item.title: [7] Phonon-dominated thermal conductivity of a superconducting amorphous MoSi thin film
item.description:
Last authors: Jacopo Piantanida Chiesa, Tom Q. Post, Martin P. van Exter, Michiel J. A. de Dood

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental thermal transport study in a superconducting thin film material.

Tags: #superconductivity #transport #thin-film

Abstract: We use the differential 3{\omega} method to directly measure the temperature dependent thermal conductivity for about 90 nm Mo0.78Si0.22 thin films. The measurements are performed in a closed-cycle cryostat to access the temperature range between 50 K and 300 K. The MoSi thin films are capped with Al2O3 and probed with a Pt wire. The results show that the thermal conductivity does not satisfy the Wiedemann-Franz law. This implies that thermal transport in MoSi is not dominated by electrons but by phonon-like excitations, contrary to what is assumed in many electro-thermal models of superconducting devices. We argue that this property might be related to the weak localization visible in the resistivity as a function of temperature curves of the superconductor.

item.title: [7] Gate-Switchable Josephson Diode Effect in Graphene via Magnetochiral Anisotropy
item.description:
Last authors: Xing He, Ruihao Zhang

Authors: Chuan-Shuai Huang, Xing He, Ruihao Zhang

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimentally relevant study of nonreciprocal transport in a graphene-based superconducting device.

Tags: #material:graphene #topic:superconductivity #topic:transport

Abstract: The Josephson diode effect originating from magnetochiral anisotropy has thus far been realized primarily in conventional two-dimensional electron gases. Here, we propose a graphene-based Josephson junction as a broadly gate-tunable platform for nonreciprocal supercurrent transport. We demonstrate that the nonreciprocal critical current not only reverses its sign when graphene is switched from $n$- to $p$-type doping via electrostatic gating, but its efficiency can also be continuously tuned from zero up to $\sim 40\%$. This gate-controlled polarity switching and efficiency modulation---unique to the chiral nature of Dirac fermions in graphene---has no counterpart in conventional semiconductor systems, positioning the graphene Josephson diode as a highly versatile component for advanced superconducting circuits.

item.title: [10] Coherence and pairing enhancement in a trilayer cuprate with layer-selective charge order
item.description:
Last authors: M. Capone, A. Damascelli

Authors: S. Smit, M. Bluschke, P. Moen, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct hit: tr-ARPES study of charge order and superconductivity in a trilayer cuprate.

Tags: #method:ARPES #material:Bi2223 #topic:charge-order #topic:superconductivity

Abstract: Trilayer cuprates hold the record for the highest superconducting critical temperatures ($T_{\text{c}}$), yet the underlying mechanism remains elusive. Using time- and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (tr-ARPES), we uncover a striking interplay between charge order, superconducting gap magnitude, and quasiparticle coherence in Bi$_2$Sr$_2$Ca$_2$Cu$_3$O$_{10+\delta}$ (Bi2223). We present ARPES-based evidence of charge order on the inner CuO$_2$ plane -- as confirmed via resonant x-ray scattering (RXS) -- and show that the same inner plane hosts a large superconducting gap matching its doping, firmly establishing it as underdoped. Despite its underdoped nature, the inner plane also exhibits an exceptional degree of quasiparticle coherence; suppressing charge-order fluctuations further enhances this, making it comparable to that of the overdoped outer planes at elevated electronic temperatures. At the same time, on the overdoped outer planes we find larger superconducting gaps than what is seen on comparably doped single and bilayer cuprates, indicating an unexpected and simultaneous enhancement of both coherence and pairing interactions in Bi2223. These findings, supported by complementary single- and three-layer Hubbard model calculations, reveal a unique interlayer mechanism in which both pairing strength and phase coherence are optimized when interfacing planes with distinct hole concentrations, providing new microscopic insight into the record $T_{\text{c}}$ of Bi2223.

item.title: [10] Surface-extended Andreev bound states emerging from intrinsic surface superconductivity of PtBi2
item.description:
Last authors: Bernd B\"uchner, Matthias Bode

Authors: Xiaochun Huang, Lingxiao Zhao, Sebastian Schimmel, et al.

Score 10/10 A_MUST_READ

Why: Direct hit: STM and ARPES context on a Weyl semimetal with unconventional surface superconductivity.

Tags: #method:STM #method:ARPES #material:PtBi2 #topic:Weyl-semimetal

Abstract: Intrinsic topological superconductivity remains one of the central open questions in condensed-matter physics. The three-dimensional Weyl semimetal PtBi$_2$ has recently been shown by angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy to host a superconducting gap that opens exclusively on its Fermi-arc surface states and exhibits a nodal structure, making it a promising platform for exploring unconventional and potentially topological superconductivity. However, despite these momentum-resolved insights, the real-space spectroscopic signatures of unconventional superconductivity in PtBi$_2$ remain unclear. Here, using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy, we reveal a sizable and spatially homogeneous gap ($\Delta > 10\,\mathrm{meV}$) on atomically pristine terraces of PtBi$_2$. Within this gap, we detect surface-extended in-gap states exhibiting pronounced atomic-scale spatial modulation. Analysis of the tunneling spectra indicates that these states are most consistently interpreted as Andreev bound states within a superconducting gap. Further phenomenological modeling shows that their characteristic spectral features are naturally captured by a chiral pairing scenario. Our results establish a direct real-space connection between the superconducting gap and surface-extended quasiparticle states in PtBi$_2$, and provide new insight into the nature of its unconventional surface superconductivity. These findings highlight PtBi$_2$ as a versatile platform for exploring exotic quasiparticle excitations and potential Majorana physics.

item.description:
Last authors: Ho-Kwang Mao, Jikun Chen

Authors: Haowen Han, Yusong Zhao, Yi Bian, et al.

Why: Highly relevant study of unconventional and reentrant superconductivity in infinite-layer nickelates.; demoted from A: broad CM, not direct user/project hit

Tags: #material:nickelate #topic:superconductivity #topic:quantum-criticality

Abstract: Recently, preliminary magnetic field-reentrant superconductivity manifested in high-temperature (Tc) Eu-doped infinite-layer (IL) nickelates, beyond analogous discoveries exclusively in low-Tc systems. This evokes intriguing fundamental issues about potential quantum-phase boundary and criticality between unconventional superconductivity and field-reentrant-one, which are inexplicable owing to formidable challenges in growing IL-nickelates towards later-series rare-earths. Herein, we open up chemical avenues to enable effective growth of (RE1-yRE'y)1-xEuxNiO2 (RE/RE': Pr, Nd, Sm, Gd, Dy), giving rise to discoveries of RE-4f-related quantum competition between high-Tc and reentrant superconductivity. Robust magnetic-field-reentrant superconductivity with uniaxial anisotropy is observed at superconducting-dome boundaries, stemming from Eu2+-4f7 associated competition between magnetic-fluctuation promoted pairing and exchange-field interactions. Their quantum-criticality is further modulable via RE(RE')-magnetism, which either reinforces reentrancy or elevates Tc (40.1 K) with more robust critical-current-density (~266 kA/cm2 at 2 K) beyond Sr-/Ca-doped counterparts. Our synthetic route enables the establishment of an ideal platform via IL-nickelates for studying 4f-related unconventional superconductivity and quantum-criticality.

item.title: [7] Observation and Control of Spontaneous Magnon Emission from Spin Ensembles in 2D Hexagonal Boron Nitride
item.description:
Last authors: Benedetta Flebus, Chunhui Rita Du

Authors: Ling-Jie Zhou, Jayakrishnan M. P. Nair, Senlei Li, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental study of magnon emission and correlated spin dynamics in 2D hBN, relevant to quantum magnetism.

Tags: #2Dmaterials #magnons #quantummagnetism #spintronics #experiment

Abstract: Hybrid systems consisting of color centers and magnetic materials provide an appealing solid-state platform for advancing the burgeoning quantum technological revolution. Exploring novel coupling mechanisms between optically active spin defects and quantum degrees of freedom is directly relevant in this context. Here, we report observation and control of spontaneous magnon emission from boron-vacancy centers in 2D hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) to a proximal ferrimagnet in the near-zero temperature limit. The spontaneous magnon emission process is overshadowed by thermal magnon effect as temperature increases, reflecting the crossover from a spontaneous-emission-dominated magnon reservoir to a thermally occupied spin bath where absorption and stimulated processes restore balance. By increasing the spin defect density, we further present that spontaneous magnon emission into a common spin bath could help establish magnon-mediated correlations in dense hBN spin ensembles. Our results are quantitatively captured by theoretical modeling, bringing insights into understanding qubit-magnon coupling, correlated spin dynamics, and many-body physics of color centers in the quantum regime.

item.description:
Last authors: Pawe{\l} Matus, Tobias Holder

Why: Theory of Wigner crystals with strong connections to CDW, anomalous Hall, and experimental probes.

Tags: #theory #Wignercrystal #CDW #anomalousHall #2Dsystems

Abstract: The physics of Wigner solids is characterized by an interplay of elasticity and long-range electrostatics, endowing crystal defects with properties distinct from those in charge-neutral crystals. Recent experiments observing lattice melting and Wigner-crystal-adjacent phases in two dimensions necessitate an examination of how defects affect the long-wavelength properties of such solids. Here, we use duality techniques to construct a comprehensive framework for studying the contribution of vacancies and interstitials, dislocations, and disclinations to the effective action of two-dimensional charged crystals. This allows for a systematic investigation of the interaction energies for the different combinations of defect pairs. We further study melting transitions due to defect proliferation, assessing and justifying some of the assumptions present in the literature. In the metallic Wigner crystal phase, characterized by a finite ground state density of vacancies, we find phonons with a dispersion relation that varies in an unusual way with the vacancy density. Consequently, we discuss how thermodynamic properties of such a vacancy Fermi liquid can be probed in measurements of the melting temperature and speed of sound. The field theory developed here can serve as a starting point in the study of anomalous Hall crystals and charge density waves with defects.

Abstract: The physics of Wigner solids is characterized by an interplay of elasticity and long-range electrostatics, endowing crystal defects with properties distinct from those in charge-neutral crystals. Recent experiments observing lattice melting and Wigner-crystal-adjacent phases in two dimensions necessitate an examination of how defects affect the long-wavelength properties of such solids. Here, we use duality techniques to construct a comprehensive framework for studying the contribution of vacancies and interstitials, dislocations, and disclinations to the effective action of two-dimensional charged crystals. This allows for a systematic investigation of the interaction energies for the different combinations of defect pairs. We further study melting transitions due to defect proliferation, assessing and justifying some of the assumptions present in the literature. Consequently, we discuss how thermodynamic properties of such a vacancy Fermi liquid can be probed in measurements of the melting temperature and speed of sound. The field theory developed here can serve as a starting point in the study of anomalous Hall crystals and charge density waves with defects.

Why: Holographic modeling of cuprate strange metals specifically calibrated using ARPES measurements.

Abstract: We develop a Neural-ODE framework to infer effective bulk metric functions and the charge-weighted gauge potential from boundary fermionic spectra within a static, planar black-hole ansatz. Controlled benchmarks recover the known bulk profiles of the Einstein--Maxwell and Gubser--Rocha models. We then use normalized interaction self-energy targets generated from an extended power-law liquid model with parameters calibrated by angle-resolved photoemission measurements to test the proposed geometric explanation of cuprate strange-metal spectra in a semi-holographic setting. For this application, we use a massless probe in backgrounds with conformal-to-$\mathrm{AdS}_2\times\mathbb{R}^2$ asymptotics and derive a spectral extraction formula from the conserved radial Dirac flux. We identify coordinate/Weyl redundancy and a degeneracy in the scaled Hawking temperature of the normalized inverse problem. The conformal factor remains undetermined, so bulk entropy and the associated contribution to electronic specific heat require independent input. Low-temperature targets are fitted accurately across the studied doping range. In the high-temperature test, however, the present ansatz and optimization search have not yielded a refined geometry that accurately reproduces the thermal spectral shape while preserving frequency symmetry. These results may guide the further development of semi-holographic models for cuprates, and the framework may also find applications in other strongly correlated electron systems.
